 Korean media reports on BigBang's concert at My Dinh Stadium.
 Besides reporting on BigBang's concert at My Dinh Stadium, Chosun also stated that the group IVE plans to perform in Vietnam in April 2027.
 ZNews • 26/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 On October 26th, the South Korean newspaper Chosun published an article about BigBang's concert at My Dinh Stadium in Hanoi. The article also mentioned that the Golden Disc Awards will be held in Hanoi for the first time in January 2027. The girl group IVE also plans to perform in Vietnam in April 2024. However, specific details have not yet been released. IVE is a popular South Korean girl group, especially known for member Jang Won Young.
 Regarding the BigBang concert at My Dinh Stadium, according to Korean media, 45,000 spectators filled the stands each night. The concert in Vietnam was BigBang's first solo performance here since their debut in 2006. When announcing their 20th anniversary tour schedule, BigBang included Hanoi as a destination alongside Tokyo (Japan), London (England), Paris (France), Singapore , and Sydney (Australia)... 
 A picture of the three BigBang members at the concert.
 In 2012, during the period when K-pop was beginning to explode globally, the group performed in Vietnam as guest artists at a music festival. However, this is BigBang's first solo concert in Vietnam. Tickets for both nights were almost sold out as soon as they went on sale in August.
 On the day of the concert, fans lined up from early morning in front of BigBang's official merchandise store. The 20th anniversary edition lightstick, originally priced at 1.7 million VND (approximately 90,000 won), was limited to one per person. However, the product quickly appeared on social media with resale prices ranging from 2 million VND to 2.5 million VND.
 You may also like "Some vendors even rented out lightsticks and performance costumes for 50,000-100,000 VND per day. The hotel, located about 500 meters from the stadium, was almost fully booked during the concert," Chosun wrote.
 The majority of the audience at the venue were long-time BigBang fans. Kpop has gone through many generations of idols, from the first to the fourth generation. However, for fans who have been dedicated to BigBang, their feelings for the group remain unchanged as they have grown up alongside their idols over the years.
 Ngoc Lien, 36, a mother of two, bought a ticket for the second night of the concert for 7.5 million VND. On the first night, she sat outside the stadium to experience the concert atmosphere. "Local fans call the seats outside the stadium – where you can hear the music without a ticket – CAT6," according to Chosun . 
 The BigBang concert attracted a large audience of Vietnamese and international fans. Photo: Viet Ha. 
 Besides fans of the same age as the BigBang members, many younger people were also present at the stadium. Min, an office worker in her early 20s, said, "I went through my difficult school days with BigBang." She added that she learned Korean thanks to the group, and even practiced Korean cheering phrases specifically for this concert.
 You may also like The BigBang members also seemed to have prepared special messages for their Vietnamese fans. Taeyang led the crowd in chanting "Vietnam champions!", a slogan to cheer on the national football team.
 According to Chosun , the event showcased new trends in the global Kpop market, which is entering a mature phase. Vietnam is gradually becoming a key market for Kpop artists to compete for top positions. This race involves both idols nearing 40 and emerging talents.
